title: Character-table evidence: bounded progression declaration audit
body:
This bounded audit checks whether the selected declarative player role/race progression tables differ between the pinned C reference and JavaScript. All 1,206 comparisons match: 1,175 scalar fields plus 31 table lengths. There are zero mismatch witnesses and zero distinct candidate causes; no gameplay change is proposed.

Coverage: 13 role attribute/distribution/HP/energy vectors and cutoffs, five race attribute-limit/HP/energy vectors, 277 skill-cap entries across 13 catalogs, and 44 innate entries across 18 tables. The source-only runner independently resolves C and JS constants, explains STR18 encodings, martial-arts aliases and C sentinels, and saves every comparison.

Evidence: `diagnostics/divergence-evidence/character-tables/progression-20261028/`.

- JS base: `b313cde5b50f3c5b5e8f622ff32418cbc1ae12be`; C gitlink: `16ff59115315917b93185d026aeefea06db9b0f4`.
- Target and controls exited 0: seven positive assertions, 16 source-text mutations detected at exact expected keys, three malformed-input rejections. Inputs, runner, outputs and execution receipts are hashed.
- Version-1 package validation passed with 26 files, `review_ready`, no pending items; committed test-layout preflight passed at `c96dc555c32556c0e7d683cdd9ff11bb1d6af4fe` using packaging tooling from the pinned JS base. `git diff --check` passed.
- Existing whole-role-table digest and skill-catalog tests overlap this audit; README documents that coverage and the additional independent constant resolution/field-level evidence. No existing tests or game modules were executed.

Limits: agreement of declarations only. Dispatch wiring, selection/compatibility, randomized initialization and progression, skill adjustments, intrinsic grants/removal, other role/race metadata and runtime exposure remain unexamined. Matching declarations are scoped negatives, not proof of runtime correctness. No excluded investigation, gameplay code change, CI dispatch, scoring, merge, or formal approval. Main retains all acceptance and integration gates.
